# Multiplayer reference

The authority rule every state change asks, and the commands a client sends to the server with the relay that carries and applies them. For how to use it, see [Multiplayer](../multiplayer.md).

## IVtCommandRelay

Interface.

Per-unit transport seam for player intents. A predicting client's modules hand a `VtCommand` to the relay on the same unit instead of changing state; the relay sends it to the authority, which calls `VtCommandRelay.Apply` on its own copy of the unit.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `void Send(in VtCommand command)` | Send `command` to the authority for this unit. |

## VtCommand

Serializable struct.

One player intent that a predicting client sends to the authority: talk to an NPC, use an item, accept a quest, place a building. Built by the module that received the call and carried through `IVtCommandRelay`; applied on the authority by `VtCommandRelay.Apply`, which re-validates everything with the authority's own state.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kind (`kind`) | [VtCommandKind](#vtcommandkind) | `Interact` | What the player wants to do. |
| Id (`id`) | `string` | Empty | Id of the definition the command is about: item, quest, recipe or buildable. Also a player, mail or slot area id. |
| Index (`index`) | `int` | 0 | Secondary number: an equipment slot, a dialogue answer index, a targeting mode or a count. |
| Point (`point`) | `Vector3` | (0, 0, 0) | World point for walking, ground-targeted item use and building placement. |
| Rotation (`rotation`) | `Quaternion` | — | Placement rotation of a building. |
| Target (`target`) | `GameObject` | None | Scene object the command acts on: the NPC or item to interact with, the crafting station, the building to demolish, the unit to attack or throw an item at. |
| Text (`text`) | `string` | Empty | Free text: a chat line, a guild name, a mail as JSON. |
| Id 2 (`id2`) | `string` | Empty | Second id: the target area of a slot move. |
| Index 2 (`index2`) | `int` | 0 | Second number: the target slot of a slot move, the targeting mode of a slot use. |
| Count (`count`) | `int` | 0 | How many items to move or drop, 0 for the whole stack. |

## VtAuthority

Static class.

Who may change a unit's state in this process. Every mutator in the package asks here first. Single-player answers `VtAuthorityLevel.Authoritative` for everything; a networked game installs `ResolveFn` at bootstrap to answer per unit.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static Func<Component, VtAuthorityLevel> ResolveFn { get; set; }` | The rule a networked game installs at bootstrap. Input is a component on the unit in question; return how much this process may change it. Null restores the single-player default, where everything is authoritative. |
| `static Func<Component, bool> IsLocalFn { get; set; }` | Yes-or-no form of `ResolveFn`: true maps to `VtAuthorityLevel.Authoritative`, false to `VtAuthorityLevel.Replica`. A networked game that wants owner-side prediction sets `ResolveFn` instead. |
| `static VtAuthorityLevel Level(Component c)` | How much this process may change the unit that owns `c`. |
| `static bool IsAuthoritative(Component c)` | True when this process owns the truth for the unit. Gate everything that must never be applied provisionally. |
| `static bool IsLocal(Component c)` | True when this process may at least predict for the unit: the authority or the owning client. Gate movement, cast bars, cooldowns and resource costs. |
| `static bool IsPredicting(Component c)` | True when this process is the owning client of the unit and not its authority: changes must be forwarded. |

## VtCommandRelay

Static class.

The two halves of a forwarded intent. Predicting clients call `Forward` from inside the module method the player invoked; the authority calls `Apply` when the command arrives and the module re-validates with its own state. Gameplay code calls neither: it calls `log.Accept(quest)` or `inventory.TryUseItem(item)` and the module does the rest. Your `IVtCommandRelay` calls `Apply` on arrival.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static Func<float> Clock { get; set; }` | Clock the rate limiter reads, in seconds. The default is real time, so a paused game does not bank commands; null restores it. |
| `static event Action<VtUnit, VtCommand, bool> OnApplied` | Fires on the authority after a command was applied, with the outcome. Useful for logging. |
| `static event Action<VtUnit, VtCommand> OnRateLimited` | Fires on the authority when a command was dropped because the unit sent more than `VtTuning.maxCommandsPerSecond` allows. Count these per client to kick a flooder. |
| `static void ResetRateLimits()` | Forget every unit's command budget, for example on a new match. |
| `static bool Forward(Component sender, in VtCommand command)` | Hand `command` to the `IVtCommandRelay` on the unit that owns `sender`. Returns false, and warns once per unit, when no relay is attached. |
| `static bool Apply(VtUnit unit, in VtCommand command, VtDefinitionCatalog catalog = null)` | Run `command` on the authority's copy of `unit`. Ids resolve through `catalog` or the shared Definition Catalog. Returns whether the module accepted it. |

## VtAuthorityLevel

Enum.

How much this process may change a unit's state. Resolved per component by `VtAuthority.Level`.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Replica` | Read-only mirror. Nothing here changes state; replication writes it. |
| `Predicting` | The owning client of its own unit. May apply provisional changes the authority will confirm or overwrite: movement, cast bars, cooldowns and resource costs. Everything else forwards a command and waits for replication. |
| `Authoritative` | Owns the truth. Single-player, the co-op host, or a dedicated server. |

### VtEquipmentSlot

The set of equipment slots an item can occupy on a unit. Used as the key for the slot map on `VtUnitEquipment` and as the source-id suffix when equipped items push their modifiers / attributes / traits (`"equipment_<slot>"`).

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `None` | Inventory-only / non-equippable. Potions, materials, quest items. |
| `Head` | Helm / hat / hood. |
| `Chest` | Chestpiece / robe / breastplate. |
| `Legs` | Leg armor / pants / greaves. |
| `Feet` | Boots / sandals / sabatons. |
| `Hands` | Gloves / gauntlets / bracers. |
| `MainHand` | Primary weapon. 2H weapons occupy this slot and block `OffHand`. |
| `OffHand` | Off-hand weapon, shield, or focus. Auto-unequipped when a 2H is equipped to `MainHand`. |
| `Neck` | Necklace / amulet / pendant. |
| `Ring1` | First ring slot. Members of the Ring family. |
| `Ring2` | Second ring slot. Members of the Ring family. |
| `Trinket1` | First trinket slot. Members of the Trinket family. |
| `Trinket2` | Second trinket slot. Members of the Trinket family. |
| `Back` | Worn on the back: backpack, cloak, quiver. |

### VtOrderKind

An order a unit with `VtUnitOrders` carries out.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Idle` | No order. The unit attacks hostile units that come inside its aggro range. |
| `Move` | Walk to a point and ignore enemies on the way. |
| `AttackMove` | Walk to a point and fight every hostile unit met on the way. |
| `Attack` | Attack one target until it dies. |
| `HoldPosition` | Stay in place and attack only what is within attack range. |
| `Stop` | Stop moving and fighting, then go idle. Given as an order, never held. |

### VtPartyLootRule

Who may pick up items that drop from a kill made by a party member. Serialized as int; append-only.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `FreeForAll` | Anyone may pick up the drop. |
| `PartyReserved` | For `VtTuning.lootReserveSeconds` only the killer's party may pick up the drop; after that anyone may. |

### VtCompanionStance

How a `VtCompanionAi` fights.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Passive` | Follows the owner and never attacks. |
| `Defensive` | Attacks what the owner attacks and whatever hurts the owner or the companion. |
| `Aggressive` | Like Defensive, and also attacks hostiles that come inside its aggro range. |

### VtChatChannel

Where a chat message goes. Serialized as int; append-only.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Say` | Players within `VtTuning.chatSayRange` of the sender. |
| `Yell` | Players within `VtTuning.chatYellRange` of the sender. |
| `Party` | The sender's party. |
| `Guild` | The sender's guild. Needs the guild module. |
| `Whisper` | One player by name or id, echoed to the sender. |
| `System` | Server announcements. Players cannot send on it. |
| `Npc` | Lines spoken by non-player units, such as boss yells. Players cannot send on it. |
